Simplicity. Speed.

BB devices are meant for businessmen or people who use their phones for things like schedules, emails, or other stuff that doesn't require a 9 inch screen and gains an advantage from a physical keyboard. The OS is pretty basic and easy to navigate, there is very little bloat to it, and it doesn't seem to "clog up" over time like many Android devices seem to if you don't regularly clean house on your memory. I personally love using BB10 for the smooth OS. Multitasking is a DREAM - switching from a web browser, to an e-mail, to an excel document feels more fluid than with a PC. I also really like the hub - BB does a unified messaging spot so you can see updates from each of your e-mail accounts, text messages, phone calls, twitter/facebook feeds, all in one spot (in chronological order). The OS gives you the ability to "peak" at the hub which will quickly/easily show you any new notifications while not interrupting what you are currently working on. It is hard to explain how the notification system is different from iOS or Android without just seeing/experiencing it.

I see people complain about the "app gap" and that is a fair point but I've only had the need to load a handful of Android apps which all work fine: Google Maps, wow armory, minecraft pocket edition. BlackBerry world app market is certainly smaller but I think that is just due to not having as many flappy bird clones for example - most major apps are available natively (Facebook, twitter, evernote, dropbox, salesforce, etc).
